classification: Retained local implementation verification or independent assessment; not production configuration or formal gate passage

output.report:
I reviewed the candidate against the spec, the design and the current source, and compared it with the recorded local test logs. The verdict is FAIL.

What works: the cutover replaces the old graph/DAG execution layer with one core. It has a hash-chained per-run journal and an exclusive hard-link object store with conflict detection. Candidates pin exact Git trees plus approved design/spec bytes in single-repo and parent multi-repo layouts. Waivers keep FAIL/UNAVAILABLE results and are bound to the candidate, and merge authority is never inferred from them. The merge adapter rechecks the core before and after hosted checks and recloses the PR on drift. Integration is observed separately from quality acceptance. Grouped code/spec review returns separate verdicts, and a missing or invalid one becomes UNAVAILABLE.

Substantive defects:
1. Implementation authority is bound to the hashes of plan.md and issues.md. Any task-status or breakdown edit blocks candidate preparation, readiness and gate execution until a human amendment. This contradicts model-led revision and the requirement that corrective work stays available.
2. Proof applicability is bound to the Node version for every gate and to the entire process.env for runner gates. Desktop evaluates snapshots in Electron's main process, so it diverges from the CLI and plugin. Unrelated session or Node changes also invalidate proof.
3. There are no action hooks and no host capability probe. Enforcement coverage is reported as 'unverified' per host rather than established per host/action.
4. The packet gate always passes. It is reused with a stale inventory, and 'reconcile' passes merely by reading documents.
5. A later, narrower verification configuration supersedes an earlier FAIL. Merely starting a job resets the expected configuration.
6. The active-run pointer is immutable, and resume throws on an unsupported current record, leaving no current-protocol recovery path.
Lesser issues: the core does not require dispositions for claims, legacy orchestration scripts still ship, a legacy projection stub remains for desktop, and any committed symlink or submodule makes a repository unreviewable.

Unverified runtime proof (not counted as defects): the live fresh-evaluator receipt test was skipped. There is no local built desktop or plugin smoke log. Tracked/ignored record layouts and cross-repo delta scenarios are untested. No retention-decision or real-project observation recipe fixture exists. The recorded runs pass 27 of 28 core tests (1 skipped), the full CLI suite (220 passed, 1 skipped), the 4 regression tests and 12 desktop contract tests. Those tests run in one process with injected evaluators, so they cannot reveal the cross-process environment problem.

findings.criterion: R1, R2 (AC1; C1 'A failed validation cannot prevent repair in an already authorized phase'; design 'The model may revise execution strategy and task breakdown within approved commitments')
findings.problem: commitments() hashes plan.md and issues.md into the implementation-authorization subject. check('implementation') at line 231 requires an authorize-implementation decision on exactly that subject. prepare (170), readiness (180) and executeGates (execution.js:196) all require check('implementation').allowed. Any status update or task re-breakdown in issues.md/plan.md (WORKFLOW.md tells the model to keep issues useful) therefore blocks all candidate preparation, readiness and evaluation until a human 'amend' decision is recorded. An amend without authorize-implementation also drops the phase to SPECIFYING. The test 'status never captures changed unapproved documents' confirms that a plan.md edit blocks implementation.
findings.fix: Bind implementation authority to promised commitments (design/spec, and plan/issues only for scope changes such as added or removed rubric mappings). Alternatively, record plan/issues fingerprints as provenance without gating. Model-revised task breakdown and status updates must not need a new human decision, while requirement/AC changes still require an amendment.

findings.criterion: R10, R18 (C4 'an attempt ID, timestamp or unrelated report alone does not invalidate proof'; C6 'CLI, native skills and desktop use the same core view')
findings.problem: executionEnvironment binds {node: process.version, platform, arch} for every gate, and for runner gates it also binds an identity of the entire process.env (only _, OLDPWD and SHLVL removed). currentResult (core.js:208-210) recomputes this in the evaluating process and rejects with 'Execution environment changed'. Desktop calls currentSnapshot inside Electron's main process (desktop/main/protocol-adapter.js:21), whose Node version and GUI environment differ from the CLI/plugin. Desktop therefore reports every result as unavailable while the CLI reports it current. Per-session variables (PWD, terminal/session IDs, host agent variables) or a Node upgrade likewise invalidate unrelated code/spec/judge reviews and verification.
findings.fix: Bind only declared, relevant environment assumptions, such as configured check executables, declared runtime inputs and an explicit allow-list of env keys. Do not bind the Node version or the whole environment for independent and assessment gates. Add a cross-process test that admits a result from a different process environment.

findings.criterion: R17 (C6 'Report per host/action whether protection was exercised, is adapter-only, or is cooperative'; design 'Implementation must establish actual interception support per host')
findings.problem: ENFORCEMENT is a static per-host object ({sessionStart:'guidance', actionHooks:'unverified', protectedAdapters:'required'}). It is not a per-host/per-action matrix with exercised, adapter-only or cooperative status. Both hooks.json files register only SessionStart. No host capability probe or supported-hook smoke exists, so 'establish actual interception support' was not attempted, and arbitrary merge or milestone actions outside the adapters remain unintercepted without a tested statement of which actions are adapter-only.
findings.fix: Probe or exercise action interception per host (e.g., Claude PreToolUse for gh pr merge) and invoke the same core check where supported. Otherwise report each protected action as 'adapter-only' or 'cooperative' per host, with a test that distinguishes mocked adapter assertions from actual interception.

findings.criterion: R7, R9 (C1 'Enter human acceptance … current review packet'; 'No substantive gate is … converted into a presentation-only item')
findings.problem: The packet gate always returns PASS with an inventory snapshot of the results that existed at execution time. Its applicability (currentResult) never compares that inventory with the current latest results. The reuse block (lines 257-275) returns the old packet for an identical request (same config/consumed/history), so a packet listing verification as UNAVAILABLE or PASS remains the 'current' packet after later results change. Acceptance never validates the packet against the evidence the human is asked to accept.
findings.fix: Make packet applicability depend on the identity of the current per-gate outcome inventory, or recompute it at milestone time. Exclude packet from equivalent-input reuse when the inventory differs, and fail the packet when its inventory is stale.

findings.criterion: R9, R11 (C1 'Model freedom cannot disable required gates'; C2 'missing evidence cannot be concealed by an old successful event')
findings.problem: Required-check applicability compares only against state.expectations[gate], which JOB_STARTED (line 35) sets to the latest requested configuration. The Verification gate has no trusted project-declared check set. After a FAIL with real tests, a later run with a narrower or trivial check set becomes the expected configuration and its PASS satisfies acceptance, and spec/judge can consume it. Nothing links or flags the superseded FAIL. Conversely, merely starting a job (even one that aborts or is a diagnostic second opinion with another model) resets expectations and invalidates earlier qualifying proof.
findings.fix: Bind required Verification checks to trusted workspace/run configuration, or require a superseding configuration to cover the earlier failing checks (or an explicit waiver/amendment). Set expectations only from completed qualifying jobs, not JOB_STARTED.

findings.criterion: R19, R20 (C5 'reports unsupported old state … rather than becoming unusable on an old lock'; 'Interrupted resume leaves a recoverable identifiable run')
findings.problem: active() throws on any active.json whose contract differs from CONTRACT. resume() (core.js:89) calls active() first and so fails. activate() (line 148) publishes active.json exclusively and never replaces it. A future contract bump (already at gatereeve/current/2) or a damaged run journal therefore leaves the feature permanently unusable through the current operations. The guidance text says to 'establish a supported current run', but no operation can do so without manual file deletion.
findings.fix: Have run.resume-current treat an unsupported or damaged current record as retained history. Establish a new durable run, then switch the active reference through a verified, recoverable step, keeping the old record intact. Add a fixture with an unsupported active.json.

findings.criterion: R9 (C1 preserve 'record reconciliation' obligation; no gate silently converted to presentation-only)
findings.problem: The 'reconcile' gate's deterministic evaluator only calls core.commitments() (captures design/spec/plan/issues) and returns PASS. No reconciliation of records (issues/tracker status vs. implemented scope) is performed. The existing lint_issues.py/lint_tracker.py helpers are unused, so the obligation passes whenever the files are readable.
findings.fix: Run the actual record-reconciliation checks (e.g., issues/tracker linting and rubric/issue mapping against the candidate's criteria) and fail on mismatches.

findings.criterion: R13 (C3 'Verify open findings and claimed fixes'; C4 core verifies 'affected finding dispositions' are present/consistent)
findings.problem: validateVerdict checks disposition shape only. A PASS verdict may omit dispositions for every claimed findingId in input.claims and for open blocking findings in the supplied history. The CLI evaluate command (cli/src/commands/current.js:57-71) cannot submit claims at all.
findings.fix: Require a disposition for each claimed finding and each open blocking history finding before admitting PASS, and add a --claims option to the CLI.

findings.criterion: R19 (AC8 'one current protocol without a legacy execution/replay path')
findings.problem: Old orchestration helpers remain distributed with no current consumer: boundary_retry.py ('portable boundary retry coordinator' with caller-supplied evidence_paths finalization), boundary_gate.py, boundary_packet.py, feature_final.py, and the agent-workflows judge/advisory bundles. A model can still invoke this dormant parallel path directly.
findings.fix: Remove the legacy orchestration scripts and bundles from the inventory and package, or reduce them to helpers that the current core actually uses.

findings.criterion: R18 (C6 'Remove incidental ordering controls and legacy execution choices')
findings.problem: currentSnapshot emits a legacy-shaped projection stub (slices, boundaryAttempts, finalizationAttempts, activeSliceId) that only the old desktop consumers still read (renderer/presentation.js:165-171, main/notification-observer.js:51). renderer/dependency-diagram.js remains shipped but is no longer imported.
findings.fix: Remove the stub and migrate or remove the remaining consumers and the orphaned dependency diagram.

findings.criterion: R3 (AC2 supported layouts must finish local review)
findings.problem: Any committed symlink (mode 120000) or submodule entry anywhere in a pinned tree aborts candidate preparation for the whole repository. Common real repositories therefore cannot be reviewed, although the spec only requires rejecting path substitution during capture.
findings.fix: Capture committed symlinks and gitlinks as typed data (target or commit identity) without following them, or report them as explicit coverage limitations instead of rejecting the repository.

rubric.evidence: All four milestones are enforced in core.js check()/pass() (lines 222-285). Tests cover the implementation block, the acceptance block, merge without authority and completion with integration. However, implementation authority binds plan.md/issues.md (core.js:107,231), so ordinary issue/plan updates block prepare/ready/execute (repair blocked).

Readiness appends READY only (core.js:176-182) and the test shows no launch over 7 declarations. There is no round counter, and spec/judge genuinely require consumed Verification (execution.js:210-213). No alternate-order test exists, and plan revision triggers the authority block (see R1).

Parent no-Git with nested repo and repo-local untracked records are tested, and completion runs without evidence commits (current-core.test.js:70-78, 282-309). Tracked/ignored layouts are untested (unverified). Repositories with committed symlinks or submodules cannot be pinned (evidence.js:29).

The candidate binds per-repo base/head file blobs, raw design/spec bytes and the authorization event (evidence.js:80-104). contentIdentity is used at admission (core.js:218). The delta rejects changed requirements/criteria (execution.js:235). Tests cover drift, multi-repo invalidation and foreign feature.

localPath/components/readSafe reject traversal, symlinks and swaps (store.js:10-50), with tests. The reviewer view holds only pinned source, base, requirements and evidence, read-only (execution.js:53-88). Codex read-only sandbox and Claude Read/Glob/Grep tools still permit reads outside the view (an adapter limitation; not runtime-verified).

Exclusive hard-link publish, a conflict check and corrupt-object detection (store.js:67-103). Journal hash chain and operation reconciliation, job claim and the uncertain-job UNAVAILABLE path, and the missing-object completion block are all tested. Keep/archive/discard retention exists only as policy prose (EVIDENCE-PACKETS.md:23-25), with no fixture.

Closure validation at check (core.js:237), dirty/HEAD source checks (evidence.js:70-79,120-124) and PR sync in prepareMerge (actions.js:36-41). No evidence commit is required. The packet gate always passes and is reused with a stale inventory (execution.js:257-275,363-379).

Code/spec share one execution with separately validated verdicts. A missing verdict becomes UNAVAILABLE and an inherited context is rejected (execution.js:113-120,299-309), tested with a fake evaluator. The live evaluator receipt test was skipped (verification log), so runtime proof is unverified.

All C1 obligations appear in GATES (contracts.js:40-55). Runner receipts come from actual exec. However, 'reconcile' performs no reconciliation (execution.js:356), 'packet' always passes, and a narrower later verification configuration can supersede a FAIL (core.js:200-203, 34-36).

Equivalent-input reuse works in-process (tests show reused:true and launch counts). However, applicability binds the Node version for all gates and the whole process.env for runners (environment.js:37-54; core.js:208-210), so unrelated session or process differences, including desktop/Electron, force reruns. Starting any job resets expectations.

contentIdentity covers all repo files and requirements. Runtime input trees and executables are hashed, and pattern rule changes, consumed proof recursion and validUntil are checked (core.js:204-219). Tests cover source, dependency, pattern, scratchpad and multi-repo mutations.

Delta requires an independent single gate, a passing prior from the same run, coverage of all changedPaths, interactions and no limitations (execution.js:186-189,229-240; core.js:213-217). Prior provenance is kept, and a new SHA with identical content is not invalidated. There is no cross-repo or shared-helper delta scenario test.

History is bounded to 64 same-run review results and claims to 128 labeled findingId/claim pairs. Raw chat is excluded and the instructions treat priors as data (execution.js:214-227). The core does not require dispositions for claims or open findings, and the CLI cannot submit claims.

Blocking findings must cite a selected criterion or gate rule, with an in-scope path (execution.js:169-173). Nonblocking advice is allowed. Instructions require new-instance discovery. The test 'allows new supported defects' produces a FAIL on a delta.

One decision carries kind/subject/authority/reason/consequences/actions (contracts.js:71-88). Amend retains previousDocuments and can include authorize-implementation, and repeat operations reconcile (tests at lines 311-323, 461-477). Message IDs are optional and never fabricated (the CLI lacks flags to supply them).

waiverFor is bound to the candidate hash, and outcomes show the FAIL plus the exception separately (core.js:259-262). Merge requires explicit authorize-merge bound to the prepared action (core.js:149-152; actions.js:53-55). External integration is observed independently (actions.js:93-114). Tested.

Merge and milestone adapters deny when the core check fails (actions.js:47-48,71; core.js:276-279) and are tested. However, no action hooks exist (hooks.json is SessionStart only), and ENFORCEMENT reports 'unverified' per host without a per-action exercised, adapter-only or cooperative status or a capability probe (contracts.js:95-99).

CLI, plugin and desktop share currentSnapshot, and old mutation commands are removed (test log). However, desktop evaluates in Electron, where the environment binding diverges (environment.js:37). A legacy projection stub remains for old consumers (adapter.js:54), the CLI lacks claims and provenance fields, and there is no built desktop/plugin smoke log.

The graph, transitions, snapshot and advisory modules were deleted (changes.txt), and there is no benchmark or pilot gate. However, legacy Python orchestration and agent-workflow bundles are still distributed (workflow-inventory.json:180-264), and an unsupported current record makes resume fail (store.js:138).

resume-current uses observed approvals, preserves old files and reconciles repeats (core.js:88-104; test at line 325), and the interrupted-start test passes. Tests for changed or missing requirements and missing authority are absent, and the immutable active pointer prevents recovery from an unsupported or damaged run.

Receipts keep start/complete times, and tokens/cost are recorded as null (unknown) (execution.js:341). Exceptions are displayed separately from outcomes in desktop (current-view.js:58). There is no documented observation recipe beyond WORKFLOW.md:75-78 and no receipt/view test for unknown metrics.
